final_prompt:
I'm preparing a product requirements document (PRD) for adding team workspaces to a B2B note-taking app. The readers are engineering and design leads. They will use it at a kickoff meeting. Write the PRD as a standard PRD of about 2 pages at most.

Scope of v1:
- In: creating a workspace, inviting members by email, shared notes.
- Roles: admin and member only.
- Out: billing changes, SSO, guest access.

Open questions. List these under an "Open questions" section and leave them unresolved. Do not recommend an answer:
- How existing shared notes migrate into workspaces.
- Whether sharing across workspaces is supported.

Problem statement and evidence: I have no problem statement or evidence to give you. Do not invent customer quotes, data, pain points, or user descriptions. Put a clearly marked "Gap: to be filled" placeholder in the Problem and Evidence sections. Use one line each to say what the team needs to supply there.

Success metric: the target is 20% of paid accounts creating a workspace within 60 days. Use it exactly as written. If you add any other metrics, label each one "Proposed" so they can't be mistaken for decided targets.

Sections: Overview, Problem (gap), Evidence (gap), Goals and success metrics, Scope (in, out, roles), Requirements for the three in-scope features, Open questions, Next steps for the kickoff. Write requirements as concrete, testable statements. Include only what the scope above supports. Keep the product context to what I stated and do not add details about the company's stage or its users.

Mark anything you had to assume with "Assumption:" inline, so I can review each one.

Reply with the PRD only, then stop. Add no preamble and no closing commentary.
